title: an identifier may begin with a Unicode letter
rule: An identifier begins with a Unicode letter or underscore (`_`) and continues with letters, digits, or underscores.

title: identifiers are case-sensitive
rule: Identifiers are case-sensitive: `Foo`, `foo`, and `FOO` are distinct.

title: string and String name the same type
rule: The lowercase keyword `string` and the standard-library type name `String` name the same type — they are interchangeable in source.

title: the bare underscore cannot be declared as a local's name
rule: The bare underscore `_` is not an identifier — never declarable and never readable as a name; `var _ := e;` is a compile error.

title: an identifier merely containing an underscore is ordinary
rule: Identifiers merely containing underscores (`_camelCase`, `snake_case`, `_f`) are ordinary identifiers; only the bare single-character token is reserved.

title: a parameter cannot be named the bare underscore
rule: The bare underscore `_` is never declarable as a name; every declaration named `_` — including a method parameter — is a compile error naming the sanctioned forms (§17.13).

title: a named parameter is an ordinary declaration
rule: An identifier merely containing an underscore is ordinary; a properly named parameter is unaffected by the discard rule.

title: a bare underscore cannot be read as a value
rule: The bare underscore is never readable as a name; a bare `_` in expression position is a compile error — `_` is not a value, so no such read can resolve (§17.13).

title: reading an ordinary local in expression position is legal
rule: A bare underscore cannot be read as a value; an ordinary literal read in the same position is unaffected.

title: a reserved keyword cannot be used as an identifier
rule: Reserved words may not be used as identifiers, except for the contextual keywords listed in Appendix B which have meaning only in specific syntactic positions.

title: an identifier that merely resembles a keyword is legal
rule: Reserved words may not be used as identifiers; a spelling that is not itself a reserved word is unaffected.

title: a contextual keyword is an ordinary identifier outside its position
rule: Contextual keywords have meaning only in specific syntactic positions; used elsewhere they are ordinary identifiers.

title: Exception is a PascalCase name, not a keyword
rule: Type identifiers like `Object`, `Array`, and `Exception` are not keywords; they are PascalCase names defined in the standard library.

title: block comments do not nest
rule: `/* ... */` — block comment, does not nest.

title: a method's end label matching its name is accepted
rule: Named constructs — method bodies included — take the identifier as the optional end label: `end methodName;`.

title: a method's end label that mismatches its name is rejected
rule: The optional label is the identifier: `end methodName;`. A mismatch is a compile error.

title: a constructor closed with the wrong introducing keyword is rejected
rule: Keyword-labelled constructs are labelled by the keyword that introduced the block (`end constructor;`, `end destructor;`); a label that does not match the construct's introducing keyword is a compile error.

title: a constructor closed with its own introducing keyword is accepted
rule: Keyword-labelled constructs are labelled by the keyword that introduced the block: `end constructor;`.

title: a labeled loop closed with the unlabeled keyword form is rejected
rule: A loop carrying a loop label is a named construct; the keyword closer (`end for;`) is rejected once the loop is labeled.

title: a labeled loop closed with its own label is accepted
rule: A loop carrying a loop label is a named construct; its closer is `end label;` or the unlabelled `end;`.

title: a nested loop cannot reuse an enclosing loop's label
rule: A loop label duplicates no loop label in scope at its declaration (Appendix C.5).

title: a nested loop with a distinct label is accepted
rule: A loop label duplicates no loop label in scope at its declaration; a distinct inner label is unaffected.

title: a dotted module name is one unnested identifier
rule: A module name is a single identifier or a sequence of identifiers separated by dots. The dotted form is a single name; it does not establish nesting.

title: an import alias is usable as a type qualifier
rule: An import may bind a file-scoped alias: `import BankingApp.Transactions as Tx;` — thereafter `Tx.Ledger` names that module's public `Ledger`.

title: naming a type requires importing its declaring module
rule: All other library modules require explicit `import` — importing `System.Threading` is required to name `CancellationTokenSource`.

title: naming a type is admitted once its module is imported
rule: All other library modules require explicit `import`; once imported, naming the type is admitted.

title: a duplicate plain import of the same module is idempotent
rule: A duplicate plain `import` of a module already imported in the same file is idempotent: the later occurrence adds nothing and is not diagnosed.

title: a current-module declaration shadows a same-named auto-imported name
rule: A declaration in the current module shadows any same-named import for bare-name purposes (the import stays reachable by qualifier) — the same shadowing already specified for auto-imported names.

title: an import alias cannot collide with a type declared in the module
rule: An alias may not collide with another alias, an imported module's name segment in qualifier position, a type declared in the file's module, or an unambiguously imported public bare name.

title: an alias with no colliding declaration is accepted
rule: An alias may not collide with a type declared in the file's module; a distinctly-named type is unaffected.

title: a module cannot import itself
rule: An `import` naming the enclosing file's own module is rejected ("a module cannot import itself").

title: importing a distinct module is accepted
rule: An `import` naming the enclosing file's own module is rejected; importing a distinct module is unaffected.

title: an interface variable may hold a boxed record value
rule: An interface variable is a reference; its underlying value may be a class instance, a boxed record, a boxed enum, or a boxed primitive.

title: value-typed assignment copies an independent value
rule: A value type is copied on assignment; each variable holds an independent value.

title: reference-typed assignment aliases the same heap object
rule: A reference type is shared on assignment; multiple variables may refer to the same heap-allocated object.

title: a user type may not be named after a reserved primitive alias
rule: The PascalCase standard-library names of the primitive value types and String are reserved type names: a program may not declare a user type whose name is one of them.

title: a non-reserved type name compiles
rule: The PascalCase standard-library names of the primitive value types and String are reserved type names; any other name is unaffected.

title: an ordinary library type name such as Stream may be shadowed by a user type
rule: This does not reserve other standard-library type names — only the PascalCase aliases of the primitive value types and String; an ordinary library type such as Array or Stream may still be shadowed by a user type.

title: the keyword and PascalCase forms of a primitive name the same static members
rule: Static members of the standard library type are accessible through either form: int.Parse, int.MaxValue, double.IsNaN.

title: the ordering operators on bool operands are a compile error
rule: Ordering (<, <=, >, >=) on every primitive except bool — the ordering operators on bool operands are a compile error.

title: the ordering operators on int operands compile
rule: Ordering (<, <=, >, >=) on every primitive except bool.

title: bitwise operators on bool operands are a compile error
rule: Bitwise (&, |, ^, ~) ... Not valid on bool, char, or floating-point types. Boolean operations use and/or/not, which short-circuit and have boolean-only semantics.

title: bitwise operators on int operands compile
rule: Bitwise (&, |, ^, ~) on byte, sbyte, short, ushort, int, uint, long, ulong.

title: default(int) is defined as the zero value
rule: defaultable classifies types for which default(T) is defined: every non-nullable value type whose components are recursively defaultable — the primitives among them.

title: default of a non-nullable reference type is a compile error
rule: Not defaultable: non-nullable reference types.

title: default of the nullable form of a reference type is null
rule: defaultable classifies types for which default(T) is defined: every nullable type T?.

title: a constructor-only record is not defaultable
rule: constructor-only classifies records declaring a constructor carrying a contract clause; such a record is not defaultable.

title: a record with no contract clause on its constructor is defaultable
rule: a record all of whose declared fields are defaultable and which is not constructor-only is defaultable.

title: auto-hashable records get a synthesized structural equality operator
rule: auto-hashable classifies records and value-like choices for which =, GetHashCode, and ToString are synthesized.

title: bool renders as True or False
rule: bool has two values, true and false.

title: an if condition of a non-bool type is a compile error
rule: Conditions of if/elif and while, and a case/catch arm's when guard, require bool.

title: an if condition of type bool compiles
rule: Conditions of if/elif and while require bool.

title: byte.MaxValue is 255
rule: byte | 8, unsigned | 0 to 255.

title: an out-of-range unsuffixed integer literal in an untyped context is a compile error
rule: In an untyped context, an unsuffixed integer literal exceeding int's range is a compile error directing to a suffix.

title: the same literal at a declared long target is a target-typed integer constant
rule: an unsuffixed integer literal whose value exceeds int's range is admitted at a declared integer target whose range contains it, taking that target's type.

title: a suffixed literal exceeding its suffix's range is a compile error
rule: A suffixed integer literal whose value does not fit the suffix's type is a compile error.

title: the same value under the ulong suffix fits
rule: A suffixed integer literal whose value fits the suffix's type is admitted (5000000000U exceeds uint's range — write 5000000000UL).

title: the boundary carve-out admits int.MinValue's magnitude as unary minus's immediate operand
rule: The decimal literal of magnitude 2^31 (unsuffixed) is admitted only as the immediate operand of unary -, denoting int.MinValue.

title: the same magnitude without the immediate unary-minus position overflows int's range
rule: Anywhere else those magnitudes remain errors — the magnitude alone overflows before the - applies.

title: floating-point division by zero produces infinity rather than raising
rule: floating-point division by zero produces one of these [Infinity, -Infinity, NaN] rather than raising an exception.

title: zero divided by zero produces NaN
rule: floating-point division by zero produces one of Infinity, -Infinity, or NaN rather than raising an exception.

title: a floating-point literal exceeding the type's largest finite value is a compile error
rule: a literal whose magnitude exceeds its type's largest finite value (1e999, or 1e40f against float) is a compile error.

title: a floating-point literal within range compiles
rule: A floating-point literal denotes the nearest representable value of its type, provided its magnitude does not exceed the type's largest finite value.

title: NaN equals NaN under reflexive equality
rule: NaN = NaN is true.

title: negative zero equals positive zero
decimal division by zero raises DivideByZeroException
rule: Division by zero raises DivideByZeroException.

title: decimal arithmetic exactly represents finite decimal fractions
rule: High-precision decimal floating-point ... Exact representation of finite decimal fractions.

title: char values compare by code-point value
rule: Character values compare by code-point value: 'A' < 'B'.

title: a surrogate code point is not a valid char value
rule: Surrogate code points (U+D800 to U+DFFF) are not valid char values.

title: a non-surrogate char literal compiles
rule: A single Unicode scalar value, 32 bits wide; surrogate code points are not valid char values, other code points are.

title: string Length returns the number of code points
rule: s.Length returns the number of code points in s. O(1).

title: string indexing returns the char at a zero-indexed code-point position
rule: s[i] returns the char at code-point position i, zero-indexed. O(1).

title: out-of-range string indexing raises IndexOutOfRangeException
rule: s[i] ... Out-of-range raises IndexOutOfRangeException.

title: a closed range slice includes both endpoints
rule: s[r] ... a closed s[a..b] includes both ends.

title: a half-open range slice excludes the upper endpoint
rule: s[r] ... a half-open s[a..<b] excludes the upper.

title: an open-ended range slice extends to the end of the string
rule: s[r] ... the open-ended forms (s[..b], s[a..], s[..]) extend to the start or end of the string.

title: string ordering requires non-nullable operands
rule: Ordering requires non-nullable operands: an operand of static type string? is a compile error.

title: string ordering with non-nullable operands compiles
rule: Ordering requires non-nullable operands.

title: the + operator performs no implicit ToString conversion
rule: The compiler does not implicitly convert other types to string; use interpolation or .ToString().

title: interpolation is the correct way to embed a non-string value
rule: The compiler does not implicitly convert other types to string; use interpolation or .ToString().

title: a method with no declared return type has the unit-type result
rule: () is the type with exactly one value, also written (). It is the return type of methods declared without an explicit return type.

title: IntPtr is available without an explicit import
rule: IntPtr and UIntPtr are compiler intrinsics ... These types live in the auto-imported System module.

title: sbyte does not implicitly convert to byte (same-width signed/unsigned)
rule: The following are never implicit: between signed and unsigned types of the same or narrower width (e.g. int -> uint, uint -> int, short -> ushort).

title: sbyte implicitly converts to short (admitted widening)
rule: sbyte implicitly converts to short, int, long, float, double, decimal (the §5.1 implicit-conversion table). Twin of s5_1_0001: same source type, a target the table admits instead of one it excludes.

title: int does not implicitly convert to uint (same-width signed/unsigned)
rule: The following are never implicit: between signed and unsigned types of the same or narrower width (e.g. int -> uint, uint -> int, short -> ushort).

title: int implicitly converts to long (admitted widening)
rule: int implicitly converts to long, float, double, decimal (the §5.1 implicit-conversion table). Twin of s5_1_0003: same source type, a target the table admits instead of one it excludes.

title: ushort implicitly converts to int (unsigned widens to a strictly larger signed type)
rule: Widening from unsigned to a strictly larger signed type (e.g. byte -> short, ushort -> int) is permitted because no value is lost.

title: float implicitly converts to double
rule: float implicitly converts to double (the §5.1 implicit-conversion table).

title: double does not implicitly convert to float
rule: Implicit conversions occur only as listed in §5.1's table; double to float narrows and is not among the table's rows. Twin of s5_1_0006: same pair, direction reversed.

title: char implicitly converts to int
rule: char implicitly converts to int, uint, long, ulong, float, double, decimal (the §5.1 implicit-conversion table).

title: decimal does not implicitly convert from double
rule: The following are never implicit: between decimal and binary floats (float, double).

title: decimal converts from double only through an explicit conversion
rule: decimal and binary floats are never implicit (§5.1); decimal(x) for binary-float x yields the nearest representable decimal value under an explicit conversion (§5.2). Twin of s5_1_0009: the same pair, spelled through the admitted explicit form.

title: an enum does not implicitly convert to its underlying integer type
rule: The following are never implicit: between an enum and its underlying integer.

title: an integer does not implicitly convert to bool
rule: The following are never implicit: between integers and bool.

title: comparing an int to zero is the legal spelling the rejected int-to-bool conversion needs
rule: Between integers and bool, conversion is never implicit (§5.1); a comparison such as n <> 0 produces bool directly. Twin of s5_1_0012: same source, the comparison in place of the rejected conversion.

title: a compile-time-constant int narrows implicitly to byte when its value fits
rule: An expression of integer type that is a compile-time constant implicitly converts to any integer type whose range contains its value: var b: byte := 50; is exactly such a conversion.

title: a compile-time constant whose value does not fit the target's range is a compile error
rule: A constant whose value does not fit the target's range is a compile error at the conversion site — never a silent truncation. Twin of s5_1_0014: same target, a value outside byte's range.

title: constant narrowing crosses signedness when the constant's value fits the target's range
rule: The rule is value-based, not type-based: the source may be a compile-time constant of any integer type, and the target any integer type whose range contains the value, across signedness: const N: long := 8; var b: byte := N; is well-typed.

title: a run-time int value does not implicitly narrow to byte even when it would fit
rule: The [constant-narrowing] rule applies to constants only; a run-time int value still requires the explicit byte(x) narrowing of §5.2. Twin of s5_1_0014: the same target, a non-constant source.

title: a non-nullable value implicitly converts to its nullable form
rule: For any type T, T implicitly converts to T? — for a value type, the present-value wrapping.

title: a derived class reference implicitly converts to its base class
rule: Reference conversions are implicit: class to base class, transitively, up to Object.

title: a base class reference does not implicitly convert to a derived class
rule: Implicit conversions occur only as listed in §5.1; a downcast from a base to a derived class is not among the listed reference conversions. Twin of s5_1_0019: same pair, direction reversed.

title: a value type implicitly converts to Object by boxing
rule: Reference conversions are implicit: any type to Object — value types (primitives, records, enums, non-owning inline arrays, the unit type) by boxing.

title: a call applicable through two co-equal reference conversions is an ambiguous compile error
rule: For overload resolution, reference conversions rank co-equal with the other implicit conversions: given M(a: Animal) and M(o: Object), the call M(dog) is ambiguous — upcast explicitly.

title: explicit int-from-double conversion truncates toward zero
rule: var i: int := int(d); // truncates toward zero.

title: a checked integer narrowing that does not fit raises OverflowException
rule: Integer narrowing raises OverflowException if the value does not fit.

title: an explicit conversion from int to bool is rejected
rule: bool(n) remains an error in both the implicit and explicit forms — a numeric-to-bool reading is partial and truthiness-shaped; write the comparison (n <> 0) instead.

title: casting a negative int to uint raises OverflowException
rule: A conversion between a signed and unsigned integer type of the same width is a checked narrowing: it raises OverflowException when the value is not representable in the destination type — a negative value cast to an unsigned type.

title: narrowing a double beyond float's finite range yields Infinity and never raises
rule: float(d) for double d rounds to the nearest float; a magnitude beyond float's finite range yields +/-Infinity and never raises — floating-point narrowing follows floating-point arithmetic's own overflow behavior.

title: a nullable-to-nullable cast maps a null operand to null
rule: A null operand yields null; var y: long? := long?(x); // nullable to nullable; null stays null.

title: casting a null nullable to its non-nullable form raises NullReferenceException
rule: var m: int := int(n); // raises NullReferenceException if n is null.

title: an in-range int converts to its enum constant
rule: An integer-to-enum cast E(n) is checked against the declared constants: it succeeds exactly when n equals the underlying value of some declared constant of E, and yields that value.

title: an integer-to-enum cast of a constant equal to no declared constant is a compile error
rule: When n is a compile-time constant equal to no declared constant, the cast is a compile error at the cast site — the same posture as §5.1's constant-narrowing range error.
check: compile error at the cast site

title: an int-to-enum cast of a non-constant undeclared value raises OverflowException
rule: When n is not a constant, a value equal to no declared constant raises OverflowException at runtime, the diagnostic naming the enum type and the value.

title: FromUnderlyingOrNull returns null where the checked cast would fault
rule: Boundary code for which an undeclared value is an expected input branches instead of catching: every enum carries a compiler-provided static member E.FromUnderlyingOrNull(value: U): E?, which returns null where the cast would fault.

title: integer addition whose mathematical result does not fit the result type raises OverflowException
rule: Operators +, -, *, /, mod, unary -, ++, and -- on integer types are checked for overflow. An operation whose mathematical result is not representable in the result type raises OverflowException.

title: integer division truncates toward zero
rule: Division / between two integers truncates toward zero. var q := -7 / 3; // -2.

title: mod follows the dividend's sign
rule: mod follows the dividend's sign. var r := -7 mod 3; // -1.

title: integer division by zero raises DivideByZeroException
rule: Division and mod raise DivideByZeroException when the right operand is zero.

title: integer mod by zero raises DivideByZeroException
rule: Division and mod raise DivideByZeroException when the right operand is zero.

title: a compile-time constant that overflows is rejected, never deferred to runtime
rule: An evaluation fault — integer or decimal overflow, division or mod by zero, a shift count outside the §6.5 domain — is a compile error at the constant expression, never a deferred runtime fault: const B := 2147483647 + 1;.
check: compile error at the constant expression

title: mod is not defined on float or double
rule: mod is not defined on float or double; an expression of the form x mod y where either operand has a binary floating-point type is a compile error.

title: mixed int/long arithmetic promotes the int operand and the result has the wider type
rule: When operands have different types, the smaller-range operand is implicitly promoted to the larger type. The result has the larger type.

title: arithmetic between double and decimal has no implicit conversion and is a compile error
rule: If no implicit conversion exists between the operand types (e.g. double and decimal), the operation is a compile error and an explicit cast is required.

title: floating-point overflow produces Infinity rather than raising
rule: float and double arithmetic follows IEEE 754. Overflow produces +/-Infinity. No exception is raised.

title: 0.0 / 0.0 produces NaN
rule: Operations involving NaN propagate NaN. Division by zero produces +/-Infinity or NaN. No exception is raised.

title: a nonzero double divided by zero produces Infinity rather than raising
rule: Division by zero produces +/-Infinity or NaN. No exception is raised.

title: decimal arithmetic that overflows raises OverflowException
rule: decimal arithmetic raises OverflowException on overflow and DivideByZeroException on division by zero. There is no Infinity or NaN for decimal.

title: decimal division by zero raises DivideByZeroException
rule: decimal arithmetic raises OverflowException on overflow and DivideByZeroException on division by zero.

title: the bitwise AND operator is not valid on bool
rule: Operators &, |, ^, <<, >>, and unary ~ operate on the binary representation of integer values. They are not valid on bool, char, or floating-point types.

title: bitwise complement of a signed integer equals negation of the value plus one
rule: ~x is the bitwise complement; for signed types, ~x = -(x + 1).

title: bits shifted beyond the left operand's width are discarded silently and the result never faults
rule: Within the domain, bits shifted beyond the left operand's width are discarded silently — that is the operation, exactly as & discards bits — and the result never faults.

title: a compile-time-constant shift count outside the left operand's width domain is a compile error
rule: A count outside the domain — negative, or >= width — is a fault: a compile error when the count is a compile-time constant.

title: a non-constant shift count outside the domain raises OverflowException at runtime
rule: A count outside the domain ... raises OverflowException at runtime otherwise.

title: a compound assignment on a narrower integer target writes back through a checked narrowing
rule: When T is an integer type or char and R is an integer type, the result is converted back to T by the corresponding §5.2 checked narrowing: b += 10 on b: byte is b := byte(b + 10).

title: a compound assignment's narrow-integer write-back raises OverflowException out of range
rule: b += 10 on b: byte is b := byte(b + 10) — the addition runs in int per §6.2, and a result outside byte's range raises OverflowException — never a silent truncation.

title: a read-modify-write compound assignment on a nullable operand is a compile error
rule: A read-modify-write compound assignment is a compile error when the static type of its left-hand side, or of its right operand, is a nullable type — the desugared x op e has no meaning on a nullable operand.

title: ++ is not a user-overloadable operator token
rule: Unary operators have no compound forms; ++/-- are not overloadable (v0.289) — declare operator +, write c := c + 1;.

title: a compound assignment evaluates each constituent of its left-hand side exactly once
rule: Every constituent of the left-hand side's lvalue chain is evaluated exactly once, left to right — including every index expression in the chain.

title: a non-nullable reference implicitly converts to its nullable form
rule: A non-nullable reference type implicitly converts to its nullable form.

title: a nullable reference does not implicitly convert to its non-nullable form
rule: The reverse (nullable to non-nullable) requires a null check or `!`.

title: a nullable value type either holds a value or null
rule: A value type wrapped in `?` is an optional: it either holds a value or `null`.

title: assigning null to a non-nullable local is rejected
rule: Assigning `null` to a non-nullable target is a compile error.

title: assigning null to a nullable local is admitted
rule: Assigning `null` to a non-nullable target is a compile error (contrapositive: a nullable target admits it).

title: member access on an unnarrowed nullable value is rejected
rule: Member access, method calls, and indexing on a nullable value are compile errors unless the compiler has narrowed it to non-null.

title: a null test narrows the true branch for member access
rule: A null test — `x <> null` — narrows the true branch, admitting member access there.

title: an early exit on the null branch narrows the surviving path
rule: An early exit — after `if x = null then return; end;` — narrows the surviving path.

title: is not null narrows to the non-nullable form
rule: `x is not null` narrows to the non-nullable form.

title: a mutable field never narrows, even after a null check
rule: The compiler narrows local variables and `readonly` fields; it never narrows mutable fields or properties.

title: copying a mutable field to a local admits narrowing on the copy
rule: The standard pattern is to copy a nullable field to a local before narrowing; local-variable narrowing then applies to the copy.

title: reassignment from a nullable expression invalidates narrowing
rule: The narrowing of a variable is invalidated when, within the controlled block, the variable is reassigned from a nullable-typed expression.

title: passing a narrowed local as a ref argument invalidates narrowing
rule: The narrowing of a variable is invalidated when, within the controlled block, the variable is passed as a `ref` or `out` argument (the callee may reassign it).

title: a nullable readonly field narrows across an intervening call
rule: A nullable `readonly` field participates in flow narrowing, because outside its construction window it has no writer on any path, through any alias, so no call can invalidate a fact about its value.

title: a mutably-captured local loses its narrowing at an intervening call
rule: A variable that is mutably captured by any lambda of the enclosing function, and the block performs any operation that can transfer control to user code, loses its narrowing after that operation.

title: null-conditional access performs the access when the receiver is non-null
rule: `x?.M` returns null if `x` is null; otherwise it performs the access. The result type is always nullable.

title: a null receiver skips the whole chain, including argument expressions
rule: If a null receiver is found, nothing to the right of it in the chain is evaluated — no member is read, no call is performed, and the argument expressions of the skipped suffixes are not evaluated: `user?.Log(Render(x))` calls neither `Log` nor `Render` when `user` is null.

title: a null segment anywhere in a chain makes the whole chain null
rule: If any segment of a chain is null, the remainder of the chain is skipped on the same terms and the whole chain's result is `null`.

title: a null-conditional call on a null function value is a no-op
rule: A function value of nullable function type may be invoked with `?(...)`; the invocation is a no-op when the function value is null.

title: argument expressions of a null-conditional call are not evaluated when null
rule: When the function-valued operand is null, the invocation does not occur and the argument expressions are not evaluated — `handler?(Next())` does not call `Next` when `handler` is null.

title: null-coalescing yields a non-nullable result when the right operand is non-nullable
rule: `a ?? b` returns `a` if non-null, else `b`; the result type is `T` when the right operand is non-nullable.

title: the right operand of ?? runs only when the left operand is null
rule: The left operand is evaluated exactly once, and the right operand is evaluated only when the left operand's value is `null` — when the left is non-null the right operand expression does not run at all.

title: mixing an owned arm and a borrowed arm of ?? is rejected
rule: When the operands are owned, `??` is a two-branch expression whose result ownership follows the meet rule of an if/else join: an owned arm mixed with a borrowed arm is rejected.

title: marking a named owned operand of ?? coalesces both arms into one owned result
rule: `owned ?? owned` is owned (the chosen value is discharged once); a named owned binding must be marked `move` to read as an owned arm.

title: ??= evaluates its right-hand side and assigns only when the left is null
rule: The compound form `??=` evaluates its right-hand side, and invokes the setter, only when the assignment occurs.

title: null-forgiving on a non-null value yields the non-nullable form
rule: `x!` asserts non-nullness. The result is the non-nullable form of the expression.

title: null-forgiving on a null value raises NullReferenceException at runtime
rule: If `x` is null at runtime, `NullReferenceException` is raised.

title: a non-nullable field with no initializer and no constructor assignment is rejected
rule: Every non-nullable field must be either assigned a value in every constructor before the constructor returns, or given a field initializer at its declaration.

title: a non-nullable field assigned in the constructor is admitted
rule: Every non-nullable field must be assigned a value in every constructor before the constructor returns, or given a field initializer at its declaration.

title: a field initializer at declaration satisfies definite assignment
rule: Every non-nullable field must be given a field initializer at its declaration, as an alternative to constructor assignment.

title: reading a non-nullable local before it is assigned is rejected
rule: Definite-assignment analysis applies the same rule to non-nullable locals: a non-nullable local must be assigned before it is read.

title: a non-nullable local assigned before its read is admitted
rule: A non-nullable local must be assigned before it is read; once assigned, a read is admitted.

title: a defaultable local satisfies the must-initialize rule vacuously
rule: A field (or local) whose type is defaultable satisfies the must-initialize rule vacuously and is implicitly initialized to that default — `null` for a nullable local, `0` for a numeric local.

title: a bare unconstrained type-parameter field must be explicitly initialized
rule: A field or local of bare type `T` under an unconstrained parameter follows the non-nullable-reference rules (must-initialize, no vacuous `null` default), since `T` may be instantiated non-nullable.

title: a bare unconstrained type-parameter field initialized from a constructor parameter is admitted
rule: A field or local of bare type `T` under an unconstrained parameter follows the non-nullable-reference rules (must-initialize); assignment in the constructor satisfies it.

title: a nullable value type does not satisfy where T: value
rule: `where T: value` restricts T to non-nullable value types. A nullable value type (e.g. `int?`) does not satisfy the constraint.

title: a non-nullable value type satisfies where T: value
rule: `where T: value` restricts T to non-nullable value types — primitives included.

title: a nullable reference type does not satisfy where T: class
rule: `where T: class` restricts T to non-nullable reference types — classes, interfaces, `string`, function types.

title: a non-nullable reference type satisfies where T: class
rule: `where T: class` restricts T to non-nullable reference types — classes, interfaces, `string`, function types.

title: arithmetic + does not lift over a nullable operand
rule: No operator lifts to a nullable type. An operand whose static type is a nullable value type is a compile error at every arithmetic operator.

title: coalescing a nullable operand to a value admits the arithmetic operator
rule: No operator lifts to a nullable type; the remedy is `??`, `!`, or a narrowing check before the operator applies.

title: the relational operator < does not lift over a nullable operand
rule: No operator lifts to a nullable type; `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` are rejected over a nullable operand because an ordering comparison over an absent participant has no defensible result.

title: null-forgiving before a relational operator admits it
rule: The rule reads the operand's static type, so an operand asserted non-null with `!` is a non-nullable operand and the ordinary operator applies to it unchanged.

title: string ordering requires non-nullable operands
rule: `s < t` performs ordinal lexicographic comparison; ordering requires non-nullable operands — an operand of static type `string?` is a compile error.

title: narrowing a nullable string first admits ordering
rule: `s < t` requires non-nullable operands; narrowing an operand to non-null admits the ordering operator on it (narrow first, §7.4).

title: there is no three-valued logic — a bool? operand at and is rejected
rule: There are no `bool?` logical operators. `and`, `or`, `not` operate only on `bool`; a `bool?` operand is a compile error.

title: and operates on a non-nullable bool operand
rule: `and`, `or`, `not` operate on `bool`; a non-nullable `bool` operand is admitted.

title: a relational pattern over a nullable scrutinee is rejected
rule: A nullable scrutinee — value or reference — is a compile error at a relational pattern: ordering admits no absent participant, and pattern position performs no narrowing.

title: separating the null case first admits a relational pattern on the rest
rule: The absent case is separated first and the ordering interrogated on the bound value — `case n of null => …, var m: int when m > 70 => …, _ => … end`.

title: user code cannot redeclare Object
rule: `Object` is a compiler intrinsic; method bodies are provided by the runtime. User code cannot redeclare or replace `Object`.

title: a class named MyObject is an ordinary declaration
rule: `Object` is a compiler intrinsic; user code cannot redeclare or replace `Object`. A type with any other name is unaffected.

title: GetType on a class instance answers a module-qualified Type.FullName
rule: `v.GetType()` returns the `Type` value for the runtime type of `v`; `Type.FullName` renders a named type qualified by its declaring module path.

title: GetType cannot be overridden
rule: `GetType` is non-virtual; runtime type identity is fixed at allocation and cannot be overridden.

title: overriding Equals without GetHashCode is rejected
rule: A type that overrides `Equals` must also override `GetHashCode`. The compiler enforces this.

title: overriding Equals together with GetHashCode is admitted
rule: A type that overrides `Equals` must also override `GetHashCode`. Declaring both together is admitted.

title: the default Equals for a class is reference equality
rule: The compiler generates a default `Equals` appropriate to each type kind; for a class the default is reference equality.

title: null equals null under the null-safe equality wrapper
rule: `a = b` invokes `a.Equals(b)`, with a null-safe wrapper: `null = null` is `true`.

title: operator overloading of = is not permitted on classes
rule: Operator overloading of `=` and `<>` is not permitted on classes; classes customize equality by overriding `Equals`.

title: a class with no operator overload uses default Equals via =
rule: Operator overloading of `=` and `<>` is not permitted on classes; classes customize equality by overriding `Equals`.

title: = on a class invokes the overridden Equals
rule: For classes, `=` always invokes `Equals`.

title: the default ToString for a class renders the qualified type name
rule: The compiler-generated default `ToString` for classes returns the type's qualified name, the module-path-qualified rendering `Type.FullName` defines.

title: the default ToString for an enum renders the qualified type name, not the constant's name
rule: For enums, the compiler-generated default `ToString` returns the type's qualified name (the stdlib `FullName` rendering), not the constant's declared identifier. `NameOf` is the separate table that answers the constant's identifier (§10.4).

title: an enum that declares ToString to return NameOf renders the constant's name
rule: An enum may replace its default `ToString` by declaring a `ToString(): string` member; the replacement is used by every consumer, including interpolation. An enum whose rendering should be the constant's name declares `ToString` to return `E.NameOf(this)`.

title: a move-only owning inline array cannot be boxed
rule: Move-only value types — owning inline arrays (`[N owned]T` and `[N owned]T?`) — cannot be boxed. Boxing a value type copies the value into a heap wrapper, but move-only types forbid copying.

title: a non-owning inline array boxes per the general rule
rule: Non-owning inline arrays (`[N]T` and `[N]T?`) are ordinary value types and box per the general rule.

title: default underlying values are assigned 0, 1, 2 in declaration order
rule: This declares constants `Priority.Low`, `Priority.Medium`, `Priority.High` of type `Priority`. The default underlying values are 0, 1, 2 — assigned in declaration order from zero.

title: same-valued constants denote one value under =
rule: Two or more constants of one enum may share an underlying value. Same-valued constants denote one value: `Legacy = Current` is `true`, and no construct can distinguish them at run time.

title: two case arms naming same-valued constants is rejected
rule: In a `case` over the enum, two arms — or two `|` alternatives — naming same-valued constants are a compile error, the later one being unreachable.

title: a case naming only one alias of a shared value is exhaustive and legal
rule: Exhaustiveness is over the set of distinct declared values, so an arm naming either alias covers both.

title: a colon-list head outside the eight integer types is read as an interface, and rejected as one
rule: The colon list is one list: if its first item resolves to one of the eight underlying-type keywords, that item is the underlying type; otherwise the underlying type is `int` and every item names an interface. `double` resolves to none of the eight, so it is read as an attempted interface — and is not one.

title: short is an admitted underlying type
rule: The underlying type must be one of `byte`, `sbyte`, `short`, `ushort`, `int`, `uint`, `long`, `ulong`.

title: FromUnderlyingOrNull returns the declared constant matching the value
rule: `FromUnderlyingOrNull` returns the declared constant whose underlying value equals `value`, or `null` when there is none.

title: FromNameOrNull returns null for a digit string
rule: `FromNameOrNull(name)` returns the declared constant whose identifier equals `name`, or `null` when there is none; a digit string names no constant, since no identifier begins with a digit.

title: NameOf agrees with nameof for a written constant
rule: For a written constant `E.NameOf(E.A) = nameof(E.A)` — `NameOf` extends the compile-time operator to a runtime value over the same table.

title: NameOf yields the first-declared identifier for a shared value
rule: Under duplicate constant values, `NameOf` yields the first-declared constant's identifier for a shared value.

title: a user declaration cannot overload the compiler-provided FromNameOrNull
rule: Every enum carries three compiler-provided static members — `FromUnderlyingOrNull`, `FromNameOrNull`, `NameOf` — and no user declaration, a member or a declared constant, may override or overload any of them.

title: a distinctly named static method beside the compiler-provided tier is admitted
rule: Every enum carries three compiler-provided static members; a user declaration under a different name does not collide with them.

title: an enum cannot declare an instance field
rule: An enum may not declare instance fields (the runtime representation is the underlying integer).

title: a static readonly field is admitted where an instance field is not
rule: An enum may declare `static readonly` fields; instance fields are forbidden because the runtime representation is the underlying integer.

title: an enum cannot declare a block-form property
rule: An enum may declare exactly instance methods, expression-bodied read-only instance properties, static methods, `static readonly` fields, `const` members, and operator overloads — and no others; an enum may not declare block-form properties or properties with backing storage.

title: an enum may declare an expression-bodied read-only instance property
rule: An enum may declare exactly instance methods, expression-bodied read-only instance properties, static methods, `static readonly` fields, `const` members, and operator overloads.

title: override is rejected on an enum member outside the Object-virtual surface
rule: `override` is admitted only on the `Object`-virtual members — `Equals`, `GetHashCode`, `ToString` — and is rejected on every other enum member.

title: override is admitted on ToString
rule: An enum may declare — spelled `override` or plain — `Equals` taking the enum's own type, `GetHashCode(): int`, and `ToString(): string`; each replaces the compiler-generated default for every consumer.

title: overloading homogeneous = on an enum without Equals(T)/GetHashCode is rejected
rule: A record/enum/choice overloading homogeneous `=`/`<>` also declares `Equals(T)` and `GetHashCode` — on an enum, `override` or plain (the co-declaration rule).

title: overloading homogeneous = on an enum together with Equals(T) and GetHashCode is admitted
rule: A record/enum/choice overloading homogeneous `=`/`<>` also declares `Equals(T)` and `GetHashCode` — on an enum, `override` or plain (the co-declaration rule).

title: case matching an enum scrutinee admits the omitted prefix and selects the matching arm
rule: Inside a `case` whose scrutinee is an enum, the enum prefix may be omitted.

title: a private member is not visible outside the declaring class
rule: `private` — Visible to the declaring class only.

title: a private member is visible within its own declaring class
rule: `private` — Visible to the declaring class only.

title: a top-level type declared protected is rejected
rule: Top-level types may be `public` or `internal`. They may not be `protected` (no enclosing class) or `private` (no file-scope concept).

title: internal is an admitted top-level visibility
rule: Top-level types may be `public` or `internal`.

title: a field with no visibility keyword is rejected
rule: Every class member must declare its visibility explicitly, except the four exempted kinds. On every other member, omitting the visibility keyword is a compile error.

title: a field with an explicit visibility keyword is admitted
rule: Every class member must declare its visibility explicitly, except the four exempted kinds.

title: a destructor given an explicit visibility keyword is rejected
rule: A `destructor` is a member kind user code can never invoke or name at a use site — for such a member no visibility choice exists to spell, and it carries no visibility keyword.

title: a destructor with no visibility keyword is admitted
rule: A `destructor` carries no visibility keyword — for such a member no visibility choice exists to spell.

title: protected internal is not a valid combined visibility
rule: Bezel does not provide combined forms (no `protected internal`, no `private protected`).

title: protected alone is a valid single visibility
rule: Bezel does not provide combined forms (no `protected internal`, no `private protected`); a single level is unaffected.

title: an accessor visibility less restrictive than the property is rejected
rule: A property's `get` or `set` may carry its own visibility, which must not be less restrictive than the property's overall visibility.

title: a more restrictive accessor visibility is admitted
rule: A property's `get` or `set` may carry its own visibility, which must not be less restrictive than the property's overall visibility; a more restrictive accessor is the useful form.

title: an internal field typed at a private nested class is rejected
rule: Every type appearing in a member's signature must be at least as visible as the member — `internal _x: NestedPrivate;` is an error when `NestedPrivate` is `private`: the field's type is not as visible as the field.

title: a private field typed at a private nested class is admitted
rule: Every type appearing in a member's signature must be at least as visible as the member — `private _y: NestedPrivate;` is fine: also private, matches `NestedPrivate`'s visibility.

title: a protected member with an internal-typed parameter is rejected
rule: Every type appearing in a member's signature must be at least as visible as the member. The rule applies at every visibility level: a `protected` member's signature types must be at least `protected` — `internal` and `protected` are incomparable (§13.1), so an `internal` type does not satisfy it.

title: a protected member with a protected-typed parameter is admitted
rule: Every type appearing in a member's signature must be at least as visible as the member; equal visibility satisfies the rule.

title: an override declaring a different visibility than the base member is rejected
rule: An override must declare the same visibility as the base member.

title: an override matching the base member's visibility is admitted
rule: An override must declare the same visibility as the base member.

title: an inclusive range includes its upper bound
rule: `a..b` is inclusive on both ends — iterating `1..10` yields 10 as its last value.

title: a half-open range excludes its upper bound
rule: `a..<b` is inclusive on the lower bound, exclusive on the upper — iterating `0..<10` yields 9, never 10, as its last value.

title: mixing bitwise AND with a range operand requires explicit parenthesization
rule: Range (`..`, `..<`) with bitwise (`&`, `|`, `^`) is a mandatory- parenthesization mix: "`mask & 0..n` is a compile error; write `(mask & 0)..n` or `mask & (0..n)` to disambiguate."

title: parenthesizing the bitwise operand admits the bitwise-then-range mix
rule: The smallest legal edit of s16_1_0003 — grouping the bitwise operation inside its own parentheses ("write `(mask & 0)..n`") resolves the mandatory- parenthesization category mix and the expression type-checks as `int..int`.

title: a range may omit either endpoint, or both, to construct an open-ended range
rule: A range may omit one endpoint, producing an open-ended range used for slicing and pattern matching — the four forms `a..b`, `..b`, `a..`, `..` are all admitted range expressions.

title: open-ended range patterns match "less than" and "at or above" the written bound
rule: In a pattern, `..<0` matches 'any value less than 0' and `31..` matches 'any value at or above 31.'

title: a Range<double> is rejected — the element type is restricted to the integer types and char
rule: `T` is restricted by the compiler to the integer types (`byte`, `sbyte`, `short`, `ushort`, `int`, `uint`, `long`, `ulong`) and `char`. Other substitutions are rejected — at the range expression or the `Range<T>` annotation... `float`, `double`, and `decimal` conform [to `ISteppable<T>`] and are not admitted.

title: a closed range's Start and End are non-null, and the default Step is 1
rule: `Start` and `End` are nullable; a `null` endpoint indicates the range is open-ended on that side. For closed ranges (both endpoints present), both are non-null. ... "The default step is 1."

title: a byte-typed step silently terminates iteration on overshoot of the endpoint or of the type's range
rule: a range like `0..10 step 256` over `T = byte` constructs without error, but the enumerator advances by 256 ... and the first computed value past the start is `256`, which exceeds the upper endpoint, so the iteration yields only the start value and terminates. ... "Iteration over `200..255 step 100` for `T = byte` similarly yields `200`; the next computed value (300) overflows `byte`'s range, so iteration terminates."

title: iteration over Range<char> steps across the surrogate gap
rule: Iteration steps across the gap: the successor of U+D7FF is U+E000 and the predecessor of U+E000 is U+D7FF... `'ퟰ'..'' step 4` yields U+D7F0, U+D7F4, U+D7F8, U+D7FC, then U+E000 (the fourth successor of U+D7FC), then U+E004, U+E008, U+E00C, U+E010. No surrogate is ever yielded.

title: Contains agrees with the direction of iteration, not with unordered-interval membership
rule: an iteration-empty range contains nothing: `50 in 100..0` is `false` (matching Rust and Python), while `(100..0 step -1).Contains(50)` is `true` (descending and nonempty).

title: a constant-folded zero step is rejected at the range expression
rule: A step of zero is rejected at construction: a literal (or constant- folded) step of zero is a compile error at the range expression.

title: a runtime-computed step of zero raises OverflowException at the range expression
rule: evaluating a range expression whose computed step is zero raises `OverflowException` at the expression.

title: step may not be applied to an open-ended range
rule: `step` may not be applied to open-ended ranges.

title: step is not legal in case patterns
rule: `step` is not legal in `case` patterns (patterns test the written bounds; stride has no meaning). Confirmed by the grammar: `RangePattern ::= PatternBound (".." | "..<") PatternBound` carries no step clause (Appendix A).

title: a constant range whose direction disagrees with its step's sign warns that iteration is empty
rule: When the compiler can prove at compile time that a range's direction and step sign disagree (both endpoints and step are constants or constant after folding), it emits a warning: 'this range produces an empty iteration.'

title: an open-ended range literal directly in a for statement warns it cannot be iterated
rule: The compiler emits a warning when an open-ended range literal appears in an iteration context — `for var i in 10.. do ... end;  // WARNING: open-ended range cannot be iterated`.

title: iterating an open-ended range stored in a variable raises InvalidOperationException at runtime
rule: For ranges stored in variables, the check is deferred to runtime: `var r: Range<int> := (if someCondition then 1..10 else 10..); for var i in r do ... end; // InvalidOperationException if r is open-ended`.

title: an inclusive equal-bounds range yields exactly one value, regardless of the step's sign
rule: An inclusive equal-bounds range (`5..5`, `5..5 step 1`, `5..5 step -1`) yields exactly one value — the bound itself. The step's sign does not matter; the iteration produces the start, the next computed value (start ± step) is past the inclusive end, and iteration terminates.

title: a half-open equal-bounds range is empty for any step
rule: A half-open equal-bounds range (`5..<5`, `5..<5 step n`) is empty for any step. The lower bound equals the upper bound and the upper bound is excluded, so no value is in range.

title: a range pattern rejects a nullable scrutinee
rule: a range pattern rejects a nullable scrutinee — keyed on the pattern's kind, the open-ended and fully open forms with the closed ones ... range membership is an ordering test, and ordering admits no absent participant.

title: a constant reversed range pattern warns that it never matches
rule: Because a constant reversed range pattern can never match, the compiler emits a warning at the pattern ('this pattern never matches — bounds are reversed').

title: v in r over a nullable v is rejected for every range test
rule: `v in r` over a nullable `v` is rejected alike [as the range-pattern case], both for one reason: range membership is an ordering test, and ordering admits no absent participant... so `n in 1..5` over an `int?` is rejected.

title: digit separators are ignored and integer suffixes are case-insensitive
rule: `1_234_567` // digit separators allowed except at start/end and "Suffixes are case-insensitive: `L`/`l`, `U`/`u`, `F`/`f`, `M`/`m`."

title: an untyped integer literal that exceeds int's range without an L suffix is rejected
rule: The compiler does not silently promote integer literals: in an untyped context `3_000_000_000` is a compile error without an `L` suffix.

title: a suffix-less over-int literal is admitted at a written integer target whose range contains it
rule: The smallest legal edit of s18_1_0002 — ascribing the target type — is admitted: "(At a written integer target whose range contains it the literal is admitted at the target type — §4.2's target-typed integer constant.)"

title: the boolean literal true renders as the four-character text True
rule: `true`, `false`, `null`. are the boolean and null literals; the boolean's rendering is `bool.ToString()`, normative in stdlib §9.4: "public pure method ToString(): string; // 'True' or 'False'".

title: a full-code-point char escape resolves to its numeric code point
rule: `'\U0001F600'` // 8 hex digits, full code point range is an admitted char literal form; converting it to `int` yields the code point's decimal value (stdlib: "`I(c)` for `char` `c` ... converts the code-point value").

title: a char escape resolving to a surrogate code point is a compile error
rule: Escape sequences resolving to U+D800–U+DFFF are compile errors.

title: a non-verbatim string literal processes its escape sequences
rule: \Line 1\\nLine 2\"      // escapes processed"

title: a null interpolation hole renders the four characters null
rule: An interpolation hole renders `ToString()`; a null hole renders the four characters `null`.

title: a format spec on a double dispatches to ToString(format) with exact fixed-point rendering
the P1 format spec renders a percentage with one decimal
the X format spec renders an integer in uppercase hex
positive alignment right-aligns and negative alignment left-aligns in a field of the given width
rule: Alignment is an integer, optionally negated; positive right-aligns in a field of that width, negative left-aligns. Example: "`$\"|{name,20}|\"` // right-aligned in 20-character field".

title: alignment and a format spec compose as {expression,alignment:format}
rule: `{expression,alignment:format}` with example "`$\"{amount,12:F2}\"`" — the F2-formatted "1234.50" (7 characters) right-aligned in a 12-character field pads with 5 leading spaces.

title: a hole without a format spec dispatches to the value's ordinary ToString()
rule: A hole without a format spec formats via the value's ordinary `ToString()` (§8.5).

title: a format spec dispatches to ToString(format); a user type opts in via IFormattable
rule: A hole with a format spec dispatches to `ToString(format: string)`: ... a user type opts in by implementing the auto-imported interface `IFormattable`.

title: a format spec on a non-formattable, non-IFormattable operand is a compile error
rule: A format spec on an operand whose type is neither intrinsically formattable nor `IFormattable` is a compile error naming this rule.

title: a null nullable hole with a format spec renders the padded text null, without invoking the spec
rule: When the value is `null` at render time, the hole renders as the four-character text `null` ... A format spec on a nullable-typed hole is checked at compile time against the non-nullable form ... and the spec is simply not invoked when the value is null. The alignment applies to the rendered text `null` exactly as to any other rendered text. Worked example: `var x: double? := null; Console.WriteLine($"[{x,8:F2}]"); // prints: [    null]`.

title: a present nullable hole with a format spec dispatches ordinarily
rule: Continuing s18_5_0010's worked example: "`x := 3.0; Console.WriteLine($ \"[{x,8:F2}]\"); // prints: [    3.00] — present value: ordinary dispatch`."

title: an indexer inside a hole needs no parenthesization before a format spec
rule: the alignment `,` and the format-spec `:` are recognized only at the top nesting level of the hole ... Consequently `{d[k]:F2}` needs no parenthesization tricks (`[…]` nests its colon).

title: an unescaped closing brace that does not close a hole is a compile error
rule: An unescaped `}` that does not close a hole is a compile error; write `}}` for a literal closing brace.

title: a doubled brace in an interpolated string renders as a single literal brace
rule: In interpolated strings ... a doubled brace denotes a literal brace: `{{` produces `{`, `}}` produces `}`.

title: an unrecognized format specifier raises FormatException at runtime
rule: An unrecognized specifier at runtime raises `FormatException` (the defined-fault rule, stdlib §2.18).

title: a verbatim string suppresses escape processing — backslashes are literal
rule: A `@` prefix suppresses escape processing. Example: `var path := @"C:\Users\Bezel\Program.bzl";` — the backslashes are literal characters, not escape introducers.

title: a doubled quote inside a verbatim string produces a single embedded quote
rule: Inside a verbatim string, `\\"` produces a single `\"`."

title: an interpolated verbatim string combines suppressed escapes with interpolation holes
rule: `$@` combines both — escape suppression and interpolation. Example: `var documentPath := $@"C:\Users\{user}\Documents\report.pdf";` renders the backslashes literally and substitutes the hole.

title: the \x escape greedily consumes up to 4 hex digits as a single code point
rule: The `\\x` escape greedily consumes the maximum number of valid hexadecimal digits, up to 4. In the string `\\\x41BC\"`, the escape is `\\x41BC` (U+41BC), not `\\x41` followed by `BC`."

title: concatenation is the remedy to write a two-digit hex escape followed by literal characters
rule: To produce the two-digit escape `\\x41` followed by the literal characters `BC`, use concatenation (`\\\x41\" + \"BC\"`) or the `\\u` form."

title: a \u escape resolving to a surrogate code point in a string literal is a compile error
rule: Surrogate escapes (U+D800–U+DFFF) are compile errors. (distinct from s18_3_0002's char-literal instance of the same rule: here the escape occurs inside a string literal.)

title: a case with no scrutinee expression is a syntax error
rule: `case` always takes a scrutinee; a `case` written with no scrutinee expression is a syntax error — a ladder of conditions is an if/elif chain instead.

title: a case with no of delimiter is a syntax error
rule: The keyword `of` terminates the scrutinee and introduces the arms. A missing `of` is a syntax error at the first arm token; the diagnostic names the delimiter.

title: return inside an arm exits the enclosing callable, not the arm
rule: `return` inside an arm exits the enclosing callable, not the arm. `case` cannot be exited "early" via `return`; restructure into helper methods.

title: an arm result may not mark the scrutinee's own binding
rule: An arm result marking the scrutinee's own binding is always rejected by the consume-site freeze — the scrutinee borrow is live through the selected arm's completion.

title: a binding may not appear inside an alternative pattern list
rule: In an alternative list, every member must be binding-free — a constant, a payload-free choice case, a range, or a relational pattern — so a binding (`var c`) cannot appear inside an alternative list.

title: a binding-free alternative list matches any listed member
rule: `2 | 3 | 4 | 5` matches any of these — every member of an alternative list must be binding-free: a constant, a payload-free choice case, a range, or a relational pattern.

title: a relational pattern over a nullable scrutinee is rejected
rule: A nullable scrutinee — value or reference — is a compile error at a relational pattern: ordering admits no absent participant, and pattern position performs no narrowing.

title: a range pattern over a nullable scrutinee is rejected
rule: The nullable-scrutinee rejection at a relational pattern applies alike at a range pattern; the rejection is keyed on the kind of pattern, not on which bounds are written.

title: a relational pattern admits only the four ordering operators
rule: A relational pattern is `> 70`, `< 50`, `<= 100`, `>= 0` — these four operators only.

title: a destructuring slot list may not mix positional and named slots
rule: A slot list is either positional or named, never mixed in one pattern; mixing is a compile error naming the rule.

title: a named destructuring slot interrogates the member by name
rule: A named slot is `Identifier "=" Pattern`; the `=` is the interrogation reading of §8.4, not an assignment — "is `Width` 3?" — and a slot list may be written entirely by name.

title: range, relational, and constant patterns select by value in order
rule: A leading `-` on a numeric literal is part of the constant pattern; ranges are inclusive (`90..100`) or exclusive (`0..<60`), open-ended (`31..`, `..<0`), or fully open (`..`); a relational pattern compares under the scrutinee's ordering; arms are tried in textual order and the first match wins.

title: an unbound type pattern subtype-matches a reference-typed scrutinee
rule: Type patterns without binding — `string`, `int`, `Dog` — subtype match: a `Dog` value matches an `Animal` pattern. Subtype matching is a property of reference-typed scrutinees.

title: individual positions of a positional destructure may be discarded
rule: The type name followed by parenthesized bindings matches the type and binds positional fields by position; individual positions may be discarded with `_` — `Point(_, y)`.

title: an unconstrained var pattern matches any value and binds it
rule: **Var patterns:** `var t`. Matches any value, binds it.

title: a discard used as a top-level catch-all arm must be last
rule: When used as a top-level pattern (a catch-all arm), `_` must be the last arm; placing it earlier is a compile error.

title: a discard as the last arm is the idiomatic catch-all
rule: `_` is the idiomatic spelling of an arm that matches everything; when used as a top-level pattern it must be the last arm.

title: classes have no positional-destructuring surface
rule: Classes do not have a positional-destructuring surface, even when they declare a primary constructor: primary-constructor parameters are not auto-promoted to public properties, and the positional shape is not part of the class's pattern-match surface.

title: an unknown name in a named slot is a compile error
rule: An unknown name, a duplicate name in one slot list, a write-only property, an indexer, a static member, or a record method or non-public explicit field is a compile error at the pattern, each naming its rule.

title: arms are tried in order and the first true guard wins
rule: Arms are evaluated in textual order. The first arm whose pattern matches and whose guard is true is selected.

title: a typed binding pattern matches only non-null values
rule: A bare type pattern `T` matches only non-null values. A typed binding pattern `var n: T` also matches only non-null values — `null` is matched only by the explicit `null` pattern, an untyped `var x` pattern, or `_`.

title: a non-exhaustive expression-position case draws the exhaustiveness warning
rule: In expression position, an unmatched value raises `MatchFailureException` at runtime; the compiler warns when it cannot prove exhaustiveness statically.

title: an unmatched statement-position case with no wildcard falls through
rule: A `case` with no `_` arm is permitted. In statement position, an unmatched value falls through with no action.

title: an unmatched expression-position case raises MatchFailureException
rule: In expression position, an unmatched value raises `MatchFailureException` at runtime.

title: an enum case covering every declared constant needs no wildcard
rule: **Enum scrutinee:** every declared constant has a matching pattern — a constant pattern naming it directly, a var binding, or `_`. A statically exhaustive enum case cannot raise MatchFailureException.

title: a choice case covering every declared case needs no wildcard
rule: **Choice scrutinee:** every declared case is covered by an unguarded arm — a payload-free case by a constant-style pattern; a payload-carrying case by a positional destructuring pattern whose every slot is irrefutable. When every case is covered, no `_` arm is required.

title: a generic closed hierarchy's leaf coverage is not attempted
rule: When the closed hierarchy's root or any leaf is generic, leaf coverage is not attempted; such a case is completable only by an irrefutable arm and draws the non-exhaustiveness warning without one.

title: a statement-position case is closed with end case not end switch
rule: In statement position `case` is an end-terminated statement (`case … of … end case?;`); `end switch;` is a near-miss the closer rejects.

title: an expression-position case atom composes inside an interpolation hole
rule: The atom is self-delimited and composes inside any expression position, including inside string interpolations; it opens with `(case` and its closing parenthesis is the terminator — there is no `end`.

title: a case arm's do block closes with a bare end and no semicolon
rule: A `case` arm `do … end` block closes with a bare `end`, taking no `;` of its own — the arm is followed by the `,` separator (or nothing, if last), not a statement terminator.

title: a statement-position case closes correctly with end case
rule: In statement position `case` is an `end`-terminated statement: `case … of … end case;`.

title: an enum-typed scrutinee omits the enum prefix in patterns
rule: When the scrutinee has an enum type, the enum prefix may be omitted in patterns.

title: the if expression selects the branch of the first true condition
rule: The `if` expression selects between values, condition-first — example `var max := (if a > b then a else b);`.

title: an elif chain performs multi-way selection, stopping at the first true condition
rule: Multi-way selection chains with `elif`, in the statement form's word order — the spec's own grade example: score 85 selects the "B" branch.

title: the else branch of an if expression is mandatory
rule: the `else` branch is mandatory (an expression produces a value on every path).

title: only the selected branch is evaluated — an unselected throw branch's operand never runs
rule: each condition and branch is a full expression with no precedence restriction — in particular, a `throw` branch is admitted in any branch position together with "only the selected branch is evaluated." Since the `then` branch is selected here, the `else` branch's `new Probe()` — whose constructor is observable — never executes.

title: a selected throw branch propagates its exception out of the if expression
rule: a `throw` branch is admitted in any branch position and "the first `true` condition selects its branch, the `else` branch is selected when none holds" — here the condition is false, so the `throw` branch is selected and its exception propagates.

title: branches of a subclass and its base class compute a common type of the base class
rule: **The common type:** the common type of branch types A and B is whichever of the two the other implicitly converts into ... a subtype into its base class or implemented interface (a §5.1 reference conversion).

title: sibling classes with no reciprocal conversion have no common type — no LUB search
rule: If neither converts into the other, the expression is a compile error directing to an explicit conversion or upcast — there is no sibling-class least-upper-bound search. The smallest legal edit of s20_0006 — replacing the `Animal` branch with the sibling class `Cat` — loses the common type.

title: a bare null branch target-types to the nullable form of the other branch's type
rule: **Bare `null`.** A bare `null` branch likewise imposes no constraint of its own: it target-types to the nullable form of the other branches' common type.

title: an all-null arm set has no type and is a compile error
rule: an all-`null` arm set has no type and is a compile error.

title: a branch needing target-typing from context, like a collection literal, is rejected in an if
rule: **No branch-level target-typing** beyond the bare-`null` rule: a branch whose form requires a target type from context — a collection literal (§15.4) ... — is a compile error inside an `if` expression even when the whole expression occupies a target-typed position.

title: a bare case construction inside an if branch resolves ordinarily, not as case construction
rule: not to subexpression positions within a return operand — in `return (if c then Ok(v) else Error(e));` the branches are operands of the `(if …)` atom (§20) and resolve ordinarily; write two `return` statements, or the qualified form.

title: elif conditions are evaluated in textual order and only up to the first true one
rule: **Evaluation.** Conditions are evaluated in textual order; the first `true` condition selects its branch ... and only the selected branch is evaluated. The second condition is true, so the third is never evaluated.

title: mixing an owned (moved) arm with a borrowed arm is rejected
rule: **Ownership.** When the branches are class-typed, the expression's ownership is the arm-meet of §28.3's producers table: owned arms meet to owned, borrowed arms to borrowed with unioned source constraints, mixed arms are rejected; an unmarked read of a named owned binding written as a branch is a borrow arm, and the marked branch `move x` ... transfers.

title: two marked-move arms both meet to an owned result
rule: The smallest legal edit of s20_0013 — marking the second arm `move b` as well — makes both arms owned: "owned arms meet to owned ... the marked branch `move x` — `x` a local binding or `owned` parameter — transfers."

title: a non-nullable local must be assigned before it is read
rule: A non-nullable local must be assigned before it is read.

title: a local cannot be named the discard
rule: A local cannot be named `_` — the bare underscore is the reserved discard token. `var _ := e;` is a compile error whose diagnostic names both sanctioned spellings.

title: a runtime const local may not be initialized from an owned production
rule: The initializer of a runtime `const` must not be an owned production — rejected, with a diagnostic naming this rule and the `using var` remedy: a fresh `new`.

title: an if condition must be bool
rule: The condition must be `bool`.

title: for over an inline array is a direct indexed loop over value copies
rule: `for` iterates any iterable source, including inline arrays `[N]T`, which support direct indexed iteration through a compiler intrinsic.

title: for over a range iterates its integer values in order
rule: `for` iterates any iterable source... and `Range<T>` values (which the compiler may optimize into counted loops).

title: a type ascription on the ignore for-loop variable is rejected
rule: A type ascription on the ignore is rejected (`for var _: T in …` — a bare ignore takes its type from context, never an annotation).

title: the loop variable is freshly bound each iteration
rule: The loop variable is freshly bound on each iteration; assigning to the loop variable inside the body affects only that iteration — it does not alter how many iterations run, nor the next iteration's value.

title: a labeled break exits the named enclosing loop from a nested loop
rule: `break name;` exits the enclosing loop labeled `name`. After `break name;`, execution continues at the first statement after the labeled loop.

title: a labeled loop rejects the keyword closer
rule: Because the construct now has a name, the introducing-keyword closer (`end for;`, `end while;`) applies only to unlabeled loops — once labeled, the keyword closer is rejected.

title: a labeled loop closes with its label or a bare end
rule: A labeled loop's `end` may repeat the loop label (`end scan;`), and bare `end;` remains valid everywhere.

title: a break inside a finally may not target a loop enclosing the finally
rule: Inside a `finally`, a `break` or `continue` — labeled or unlabeled — whose target loop lies outside the `finally` is a compile error.

title: a break targeting a loop wholly inside the finally is admitted
rule: Loops wholly inside the `finally`, and jumps among them, are unaffected by the finally/loop-jump restriction.

title: a local declared inside a do end block is out of scope after it ends
rule: Locals declared in a block are visible only until the matching `end`.

title: a method with a return type must return on every exit path
rule: A method or accessor with a return type must `return expression;` on every exit path.

title: a method with no return type uses return to exit early
rule: A method or accessor with no return type uses `return;` to exit early; falling off the end is implicit.

title: an exhaustive statement-case whose every arm exits grants totality
rule: A statement-position `case` counts as exiting on every path — so a callable may end with it, with no trailing `return` — when the match is proven statically exhaustive and every arm's body itself exits on every path.

title: return inside a finally block is a compile error
rule: `return` inside a `finally` block is a compile error.

title: throw expression as a statement raises and is caught
rule: `throw expression;` and the bare re-raise `throw;` are the statement spellings of the `throw` expression, equivalent to the expression form followed by `;`.

title: a bare re-raise outside a catch arm is a compile error
rule: The bare re-raise is valid only inside a catch arm body. Bare `throw` (either form) outside a catch arm body is a compile error.

title: a discarded non-unit expression statement result draws a warning
rule: An expression statement whose result is a non-`()` type is permitted but the compiler emits a warning: the result is silently discarded, which may indicate a bug.

title: the discard statement suppresses the unused-result warning
rule: To suppress the warning, use the discard form `_ := expression;`.

title: a bare Task-family statement result is a hard error, not a warning
rule: For `Task`, the warning is replaced by a hard error directing the caller to the discard `_ := expression;`, `using var _ := expression;`, an explicit `.Dispose()`, or `Task.FireAndForget` as appropriate.

title: a local record is declared and used inside its enclosing body
rule: A `record` or `enum` may be declared as a statement, scoped to the enclosing body like a local variable. The local type is an ordinary nominal record.

title: a local record may not carry a visibility keyword
rule: The `Visibility?` slot must be empty — a local type has no access surface, so a visibility keyword is a compile error naming the rule.

title: a local record may not declare generic parameters
rule: The `GenericParams?` slot must be empty (v1) — a local type declares no type parameters of its own.

title: a local type must be declared before its first use
rule: The declaration must precede first use; local types are therefore order-significant.

title: a class may not be declared as a local type
rule: `class` and `interface` may not [be declared locally] — a class carries ownership, destructors, and the §28 disposal machinery, a body-scoped kernel surface for no recorded need.

title: the four auto-property forms are admitted
rule: An auto-property is read-write, read-write with a restricted setter (`private set`), read-only (`readonly`), or read-only with an initializer; the compiler generates the backing field.

title: a readonly auto-property may not be assigned from an ordinary method
rule: A `readonly` auto-property may be assigned only in a field initializer or in a constructor, under §22.8's per-instance assignable context.

title: a constructor may not write another instance's readonly auto-property
rule: The assignment is admitted only through `this` for an instance auto-property — the assignable context is per-instance, so a constructor may not write another value's readonly storage.

title: readonly on an expression-bodied property is rejected
rule: On every body-bearing form read-onlyness is already expressed by the shape, and writing `readonly` there is a compile error.

title: an expression-bodied property without readonly is admitted
rule: An expression-bodied property's body is checked against the declared type; the shape expresses read-onlyness, so no `readonly` is written.

title: readonly on a get-only block-form property is rejected
